intro.title: Find Your Primary
intro.text: Answer nine straight questions on the issues that divide the two parties. Your answers will place you in the primary you belong in.

questions.context: Roe v. Wade was overturned in June 2022, and each state now sets its own abortion law.
questions.prompt: What should the law on abortion be?

options.label: Legal nationwide; the decision belongs to a woman and her doctor
Legal in most cases, with some limits later in pregnancy
Illegal in most cases, except rape, incest or danger to the mother's life
Unborn life should be protected by law from conception

questions.prompt: What should the country do about guns?

options.label: Ban assault weapons and require a license to own any gun
Respect gun ownership, but require a background check on every sale
Enforce the gun laws already on the books instead of passing new ones
Protect the Second Amendment; the right to bear arms must not be infringed

questions.prompt: What should happen to immigrants who are living in the country illegally?

options.label: Offer them a path to citizenship and end mass deportations
Legal status for those who work and obey the law, alongside a secure border
Secure the border first and deport those who commit crimes
Deport everyone who is here illegally and finish the border wall

questions.prompt: How should Americans get their health insurance?

options.label: The government should cover everyone under a single public plan
Keep private insurance, and add a public plan anyone can choose
Keep private insurance and bring costs down through competition
Get government out of health care and let a free market serve patients

questions.prompt: Which direction should taxes and government spending take?

options.label: Raise taxes on the wealthy and corporations to fund more public services
Ask the wealthy to pay somewhat more and protect the programs we have
Hold taxes where they are and slow the growth of spending
Cut taxes and cut spending; government should be much smaller

questions.prompt: What should energy policy put first?

options.label: Move off fossil fuels as fast as possible; climate change is an emergency
Shift steadily to clean energy, using incentives rather than bans
Use every energy source, including oil and gas, and keep prices low
Expand American oil, gas and coal production and end climate mandates

questions.prompt: What is the best way to make communities safer?

options.label: Move money from policing into housing, mental health and social services
Keep police funded, and hold officers accountable for misconduct
Hire more police officers and give them the support they need
Enforce the law strictly and give tougher sentences to those who break it

questions.prompt: What should the rules be for transgender minors in school sports and medical care?

options.label: Protect their right to join teams and receive care that match their identity
Leave these decisions to families, doctors and local sports bodies
Keep girls' sports for biological females; leave medical care to parents
Sports by biological sex, and no medical gender transition before 18

questions.context: In June 2023 the Supreme Court ended the use of race in college admissions.
questions.prompt: Should colleges and employers take race into account to increase diversity?

options.label: Yes, it is needed to correct past and present discrimination
Support diversity programs and outreach, but without racial preferences
No, decisions should rest on merit alone, without regard to race
No, and diversity, equity and inclusion programs should be ended

tiebreak.prompt: Your answers are evenly split. Which worries you more?

options.label: A government that does too little to help people
A government that does too much and gets in people's way

dem.strong: Your answers clearly place you in the Democratic primary. On nearly every issue you sided with the positions Democratic voters hold.
dem.lean: On balance, your answers place you in the Democratic primary. You agreed with Democratic voters more often than not, though not on everything.
dem.barely: This was a near call, and you could have gone either way. Your answers place you, narrowly, in the Democratic primary.

gop.strong: Your answers clearly place you in the Republican primary. On nearly every issue you sided with the positions Republican voters hold.
gop.lean: On balance, your answers place you in the Republican primary. You agreed with Republican voters more often than not, though not on everything.
gop.barely: This was a near call, and you could have gone either way. Your answers place you, narrowly, in the Republican primary.
